fixes.explanation: The guards aren't the cause, friend. Verse 4 says they trembled and became like dead men, so they're the ones getting shaken. The earthquake comes because an angel of the Lord descended from heaven.

No storm is mentioned anywhere in this passage. The text gives the cause: “…for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven…” A storm would be a pretty ordinary guess, and Matthew gives a much bigger reason. When he explains the shaking, he points to the angel.

The text says the opposite. The angel of the Lord descended from heaven, rolled away the stone, and sat on it. That stone doesn't stay in its place. And the angel doesn't just move it, he takes a seat on it like it's his front porch.
Matthew doesn't mention any swords. The text says the guards trembled in fear of him and became like dead men. Fear is what Matthew shows here, not a charge.
The angel says the opposite, friend. He tells the women, “Come, see the place where He lay.” They aren't told to stay away. They're told to look.

Good guess, friend, but Jerusalem isn't the place the angel names. He says Jesus is going ahead of the disciples into Galilee. That's where they will see Him. The women are to go quickly and tell the disciples.

Nice try, friend, but the angel doesn't name Bethany. The message he gives the women is that Jesus is going ahead of the disciples into Galilee. That's where they will see Him. Then the angel adds, “See, I have told you.”
Sorrow isn't in the verse. Matthew says the women hurried away from the tomb in fear and great joy. They had just heard that Jesus has risen, and they ran to tell His disciples.
That's what they do. Matthew says they came to Him, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him. They don't just look at Him, they take hold of His feet. I think they wanted to be sure He was really there.
Matthew doesn't send them back to the tomb. Jesus meets them and says, “Greetings!” and they come to Him. Then they grasp His feet and worship Him.
The women don't stand back, friend. Matthew says they came to Him, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him. The text doesn't tell us whether they said anything. They move toward Him.

No written order is mentioned. The chief priests do tell the soldiers that if this report reaches the governor, “…we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble.” What they hand the soldiers is a large sum of money.

That's right. Matthew says, “So the guards took the money and did as they were instructed.” They accepted the money and then told the story the chief priests gave them. And Matthew says, “…this account has been circulated among the Jews to this very day.”
